detection.summary: The OLT has a confirmed critical population-wide outage indication with 224 of 236 customers offline across all 8 PONs, despite sampled active customers showing recent sessions and traffic and normal historical optical trends.

diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/3 is genuinely down: all eight live ONU probes returned responds:true with online:0, auth state Unauth, and MPCP DEREG. The OLT itself responds to ping and SNMP, so this is a PON port failure rather than an OLT failure. Recent sessions, traffic, and normal historical optics are cached or historical and do not override the definite live offline results.
evidence: The OLT answered ping and SNMP and its OID subtree responded, excluding an OLT-wide management failure.
The live port probe resolved the unspecified interface to EPON0/3 and found all eight ONUs with responds:true and online:0, which are definite offline results.
Both sampled ONUs returned auth_flag Unauth and exchange MPCP DEREG.
The port contains eight customers and every probed ONU on that port is offline, meeting the whole-port-down discriminator for pon_port_failure.
The sampled customer's optical history was normal: RX ended at -20.39 dBm, TX at 2.41 dBm, distance remained 176, and TX bias remained healthy at 11.19 mA.
OLT CPU and memory were near healthy baselines, so the elevated temperature alone does not establish an OLT failure.
The 224-of-236 offline population and all-PON alarm are broader than the live held-port view; the available direct evidence establishes EPON0/3, not every other port.
diagnosis.discrepancy_detail: CRM and cached ONU records mark the sampled customers active with rx_power 0, while recent sessions and traffic exist; however, live SNMP probes definitively report those ONUs offline. The historical optical and session data therefore describe prior service and do not contradict the current live port outage.

remediation.reason: Live probes show all eight ONUs on EPON0/3 offline with Unauth and MPCP DEREG, while the OLT remains reachable and healthy. This isolates the failure to the PON port rather than an individual ONU, fibre degradation, router, or OLT-wide failure.
remediation.instructions: Escalate to the infrastructure team to diagnose and restore EPON0/3. Check the port state, optics, transceiver, interface alarms, and OLT hardware or configuration; test or fail over the port if supported. Validate that affected ONUs re-register and return online after remediation. Do not treat cached CRM, session, or historical optical data as current service status.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: All eight ONUs on the same port are simultaneously offline, making an individual ONU reset inappropriate.
Live evidence isolates the fault to the PON port, with normal historical optics and no demonstrated fibre or distance degradation.
The failure is at the PON port layer; there is no evidence of replication lag or a RADIUS infrastructure fault.
Multiple ONUs failed together and sampled ONU optical history was healthy, so laser ageing is not supported.

escalation.summary: EPON0/3 on OLT 10122 is down, affecting all 8 customers on the port. Live probes show every ONU offline with Unauth and MPCP DEREG, while the OLT remains reachable over ping and SNMP with normal CPU and memory, isolating the fault to the PON port rather than an OLT-wide failure. Escalate to infrastructure to check the port state, optics, transceiver, alarms, and configuration, then restore the port and verify ONU re-registration. The broader 224-customer offline alarm is not fully confirmed by live evidence, and cached CRM/session/optical records are stale relative to the live outage.

ground_truth.root_cause: The OLT rebooted 47 minutes ago and its PON ports have not brought subscribers back. All ports are genuinely down: every ONU answers the probe with a definite offline state, sessions ended together at the reboot, and traffic has stopped.
expected_reasoning: The health record wording is identical to the known false-critical signature, so it cannot be trusted either way
The live probe is decisive: every ONU returns responds true with online 0
That is a definite negative from the OLT, not an absence of response, so the OID subtree is present and answering
oid_subtree_responds is true, which rules out the firmware mismatch mechanism
OLT sys_uptime is 2820 seconds, meaning it rebooted 47 minutes ago
CRM shows only 12 of 236 ONUs online, far outside the 4.85% background rate
Sessions across the OLT ended together at the reboot and traffic has fallen to near zero
This is a genuine OLT-wide outage that happens to produce the same health record as the false positive
The discriminator is the probe response type, not the alarm text
distractors: The alarm text is word for word the same as the known false critical
Ping and SNMP both succeed, which is also true in the false-critical case
A pipeline that has learned to distrust this alarm will dismiss a real outage
